title: Eleven Versions and One Lost Index
subtitle: 网络信息 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 网络信息（科学与技术·网络与信息）
meta: 主题语境：网络信息（科学与技术·网络与信息）　|　核心词汇：database　|　正文 337 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 database 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1981 the librarian ① built a database that no office in the city would have funded, and she said the building was the whole of the project. The ② database, meaning the store of records and not the programme, ran eleven versions and stayed unindexed; a database, she said, is the only thing in an office that is judged by how long it is left unsearched.

Every ③ database in that office had the same lost index against it, and the ④ database at the end, meaning the one they kept for the archive and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever queried twice. A database, her assistant said, is nine parts order and one part somebody willing to search; the librarian said the searching is the part that fills eleven versions.

The programmer meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the database was the whole of the system, meaning the software and not the records. The ⑥ database, meaning the software and not any of that, is the only thing in a system that everybody installs and nobody understands; database, he said, is either something you build or the only word that means both a store and a software. He said the software is the part they remember.

By 1989 the ⑦ database had become a line in a budget, and the budget had become an argument about the lost index. The ⑧ database of the whole thing, the librarian wrote in April, was one office and eleven versions of searching; database, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to search. She said the searching was never mentioned.

The ⑨ database I remember is the one at the end, which was retired in 1997 and is still described as the oldest in the city. A ⑩ database, the assistant said in 1999, is the only thing that improves by being searched; every database, she said, is a software that has agreed to look like a store. She said the software was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 数据库；资料库（指办公室里建起来的那一个）
B. n. 数据库（指那批记录本身，与那个程序相对）
C. 固定搭配：build a database 建立一个数据库
D. n. 数据库（指留给档案用的那一个）
E. n. 数据库；资料库（抽象总称，指一间办公室的全部数据资产）
F. n. 数据库（指预算里写到、被列支的那一个）
G. n. 数据库软件（指系统里被安装的那套程序）
H. n. 数据库软件（抽象总称，指人人安装却无人弄懂的那套）

answers.why: build a database 意为“建立一个数据库”，1981 年馆员建了一个全城没有一家机构肯出资的数据库。
database 意为“数据库”，指那批记录本身而不是那个程序，它历经十一个版本而没有索引。
database 意为“数据库”，指那间办公室里每一个数据库，每一个都有同一个丢失的索引对着它。
database 意为“数据库”，指留给档案用的那一个，是唯一有人查询过两次的。
database 意为“数据库软件”，指系统里被安装的那套程序，程序员说这套软件就是那个系统的全部。
database 意为“数据库软件”，指人人安装却无人弄懂的那套而不是别的，是系统里人人都装、却无人弄懂的东西。
database 意为“数据库”，指预算里写到、被列支的那一个，到 1989 年这个库成了预算里的一行。
database 意为“数据库、资料库”，馆员四月写道，整件事的资料库是一间办公室和十一个版本的检索。
database 意为“数据库”，我记得的是末尾那一个，1997 年停用，至今仍被说成全城最旧的。
database 为抽象总称，助手 1999 年说，一个数据库是唯一会因为被检索而变得更好的东西。
